problem_motivation.content: Few alloys tolerate metal additive manufacturing thermal cycles.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, only a limited number of existing alloys are amenable to the complex thermal conditions present during metal-based AM

prior_limitation.content: Rapid gamma-prime precipitation makes high-performance superalloys non-weldable.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, many of the highest-performing Ni-base superalloys are observed to be non-weldable due to the rapid precipitation of the γ ′ phase shortly after solidification

causal_claim.content: Segregation lowers local liquidus temperature and creates liquid films.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This solute segregation lowers the local liquidus temperature, creating solute-enriched liquid films between solid dendrites

causal_claim.content: Reduced late-stage segregation improves cracking resistance.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The less pronounced segregation in the Co-rich alloys, particularly in the late stages of solidification, is beneficial for cracking resistance

mechanism_principle.content: Near-solidus plasticity makes cracking sensitive to precipitate temperature.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Just below the melting point, stresses can be accommodated by plastic deformation in the solid state, which is very sensitive to the temperature at which the strengthening precipitates appear

hypothesis_statement.content: A solidus-solvus gap over 50 degrees C should resist cracking.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: it was hypothesized that a gap of >50 °C between the solidus and solvus temperatures would increase cracking resistance

evidence_result.content: Both EBM and SLM produced crack-free samples.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The 3D printing trials with both the EBM and SLM approaches resulted in crack-free blocks and blade-shaped samples in the as-printed state
tensile ductilities in excess of 32% are observed for EBM SB-CoNi-10
